l.i: Gethæus istas! hæc mila ne precor Per Ascalonitæ superbos Quis properet recitare vicos!
Ne nostra gentes damna procacibus Præputiatæ risibus impetant.
Ne mox Philistæas per urbes Læta canat, saliatque virgo Nostro rubescens Guilboa sanguine Posthac benignus nec pluuias tibi Refundat æther: nec madescant Frugifero tibi rore campi.
Hîc hîc virorum corpora fortium Transfixit hostis, scutaq; fortior. Non texit vnguento sacrata Cæsaries, clypeúsve Saulum.
Frustra ferocis lethiferum valens Tetendit arcum dextera Ionathæ: Frustra per hostiles caternas Impauido ruit ense Saulus.
Quos prænitescens gratia iunxerat, Et vita concors semper amabiles Nunc forte Saulum mors eâdem Inuida cum Ionathane perdit.
Erant minîstro fulminis alite Velociores quum volat æetheris Tractus per altos, & volucri Gestit aues superare penna.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "saliatque" (possibly "salutatque"); "scutaq;" (the abbreviation is as printed); "prænitescens" and "Philistæas" are printed with a long-s form, rendered here as plain s. The line "Gethæus istas!" is printed with a space between the words. The apostrophe before "Quos" and the initial "Ne" are decorative, not text. The stanza breaks are inferred from the lines that end short of the margin. The last line is a fragment continued on the next page.
